page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6a.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor and built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs utilizing AMD EPYC 7H12 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage options, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng, falls into the bottom 10%, reflecting the lower clock speed of the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor. However, the multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the middle 50% average, demonstrating the effectiveness of the 32 dedicated physical cores for parallel workloads. Memory performance shows a similar divergence: while cached small-block read bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidths are weak, falling into the bottom 25%.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g6a.8xlarge is suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads that benefit from multi-threaded processing but do not require extreme single-core speed or local storage. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, Redis databases, and general database operations, all of which achieved average tier performance in benchmark testing. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense allocation of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and memory, making it a viable option for resource-balanced applications that do not justify the premium of high-frequency compute-optimized or memory-optimized hardware classes.
